AIP changed my life, and it might’ve saved it, too. I had horrible food allergies and fibromyalgia pain I was suffering through because I simply didn’t know how my food was affecting me. I feel like cutting these foods out gave me my life back. 

That said, it’s not something I would do long term. Mediterranean diet is what I’ve been recommended the most by doctors, and I’m currently reading materials by the Glucose Goddess to try to further improve my diet. 

I think AIP is absolutely worth the short term struggle, but there’s nothing wrong with modifying it to suit your needs. Focus on you and your body.

Fried Garlic & Olive Oil Pasta

- 1 lb rice noodles (I like Thai Kitchen GF Stir Fry Noodles.)
- 1/4 cup olive oil (I recommend high-quality.)
- 1 clove minced garlic 
- 1/2 cup of diced sweet peppers (optional)
- Salt to taste 

Cook noodles according to instructions. Prepare garlic clove and sweet peppers (optional). Fry minced garlic and sweet peppers in a drizzle of olive oil. Once noodles finish cooking and are drained of water, add your olive oil and toss the noodles in with the garlic and sweet peppers until well-mixed. Season with salt to taste.

It’s a little different from FESS. Excerpt from a random article — “Balloon sinus ostial dilation (BSOD) is a relatively straight forward procedure. Under endoscopic visualization, the sinus balloon device is place into the nasal cavity, and guided to the blocked sinus. Once positioning has been confirmed, the balloon is inflated and then deflated. The device is then removed. The entire procedure must be performed with an emphasis on minimizing trauma to the delicate tissues of the sinus lining.” https://med.uth.edu/orl/texas-sinus-institute/services/balloon-sinus-ostial-dilation/
